does: Cooks flour in melted butter to a paste that thickens a liquid without lumps or a raw taste.
how: Melt the butter over medium-low heat until it foams.
Tip in an equal weight of flour, all at once, and stir until smooth.
Keep stirring as the paste bubbles, until the raw smell of flour is gone.
Go on to the colour the sauce needs: pale for a white sauce, sandy for a blond one, nut-brown for a brown one.
Add the liquid cold to a hot roux, or hot to a cold one, a little at a time, whisking each addition smooth.

cues.text: The smell changes from raw flour to biscuit, then to toasted nuts as it darkens.
A smooth paste that froths like wet sand and pulls away from the pan.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the liquid before the flour has cooked, which leaves a pasty taste that no simmering removes.
mistakes.fix: Give the roux time, until it smells of biscuit.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring in all the liquid at once, which makes lumps.
mistakes.fix: Add it in stages and whisk each one smooth. A lumpy sauce can be rescued through a sieve.
